question: According to the Census of India-2011, what is the sex ratio (Females per 1000 males) of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**943**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Census of India-2011, the sex ratio of India is **943 females per 1000 males**.
 
• The sex ratio is an important **demographic indicator that shows the number of females per 1000 males in a population**.
 
• A higher or balanced sex ratio is indicative of better gender equality in the society.
 
• Various government policies and programs aim to improve the sex ratio by addressing issues such as female infanticide, gender-based abortions, and discrimination against girls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Census of India** is conducted every ten years and is one of the most comprehensive sources of demographic data in the country.
 
• The 2011 Census was the **15th National Census** of the country since **1871**.
 
• Key parameters measured in the Census include population size, sex ratio, literacy rate, and employment statistics, among others.
 
• The data collected from the Census helps in the formulation of policies and planning for socio-economic development.
